comparison: Both evaluate the same claims (C3, C39-C46, C63, C66) about OS-induced GLV ratio changes. OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED despite noting inconsistencies in night experiments and light-dependent effects. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, specifically criticizing the light/lunar aspect as 'post-hoc' with insufficient replication (single replicates for moon phases), suggesting elimination of this aspect. Major disagreement on whether the evidence adequately supports the claims.

Both evaluate the same claims (C4, C47-C59, C64, C97) about calcium imaging and neural discrimination of GLV isomers. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed validation of the imaging data and statistical analyses. Peer reviewers found the study 'interesting' with good methodology combination, though requested better explanation of methodological choices. Strong agreement on the validity of neurophysiological findings.

Both evaluate the same claims (C5, C60-C62, C65, C92-C93, C98) about field oviposition behavior. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate experimental design and statistical significance. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about 'ecological relevance' including seed origin, combining two moth species, and comparison with natural feeding damage. Disagreement on whether experimental design adequately supports ecological conclusions.

Both address overarching claims C1 and C6. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, integrating chemistry, neurophysiology, and behavior evidence, though noting the link to 'conspecific attack' is inferential. Peer review (R4) also addresses C2, C20-C25, C35 (prior work context) and rates as UNCERTAIN, requesting better explanation of rationale and connection to the 2010 Allmann and Baldwin paper. Disagreement on whether the conceptual framework adequately supports the main conclusions.

OpenEval R5 evaluates claims C2, C20-C25, C35 about prior published work (Allmann and Baldwin, 2010) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer R4 includes these same claims but rates them UNCERTAIN, requesting better explanation of the connection to the 2010 Science paper. Disagreement on whether the rationale linking to prior work is adequately developed.

Both address neurobiological context claims including C37, C87-C91. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citations and reasonable interpretations. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, specifically requesting better linkage to foundational work by Visser and Ave (1978) and subsequent studies on GLV neurobiological aspects. Disagreement on adequacy of literature integration.

OpenEval evaluated claims C26-C33 (contextual background on experimental system and timing) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific background claims.
